segments.text: Saturn is the planet with the biggest, brightest rings in our solar system.
The rings look solid, but they are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock.
Some pieces are as small as sand and some are as big as a house.
Now here is the strange part. The rings are huge but incredibly thin.
They stretch wider than the gap from Earth to the Moon, yet most are thinner than a building.
If Saturn were a football, its rings would be thinner than a sheet of paper.
Next, how can you see Saturn yourself? You do not need a spaceship.
On a clear night Saturn looks like a steady yellow star that does not twinkle.
With a small telescope you can spot the rings as tiny handles on each side.
Finally, Saturn has more than a hundred moons, and one of them has lakes.
That moon is called Titan, and a flying robot is being built to explore it.
So next time you look up, remember the ringed giant is looking back.
